correctness.rationale: The exact Fourier/forest identity reduces the claim to an all-even cluster event. A fixed number of uniformly cut labels has asymptotically disjoint descendant fringes and independent geometric Yule-size limits after rescaling relative birth times; integrating birth times gives \(1/[k(k+1)]\). Binomial-Poisson convergence yields independent Poisson size counts, odd intensity \(\lambda\log2\), and hence exact bias \(e^{-\lambda\log2}\). The previously established uniform upper bound handles diverging expected fresh counts. Verified exact recurrences agree in all 60 n/alpha cases and an additional 75 numerical, odd/even and bound checks (135 total). No finite check is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The earliest 2026 source states the forest-parity identity and finite-parameter upper and lower bounds but not the exact \(\alpha_N=1-\lambda/N\) limit. A 2014 RRT source records the known single-fringe law; another near-one percolation theorem requires diverging first-generation cluster scales and does not cover finitely many cuts. Comparison of primary full texts, aliases and published mathematical records identified no direct implication or equivalent reported result. Priority is provisional.
residual_risks: A separately formulated finite-cut Poisson multiset limit may occur in older recursive-tree fragmentation or Yule-mutation literature and would require human historical-priority checking.
The single-cut law and exact forest representation are already known and are not claimed as original.

value.rationale: The exact near-perfect-memory window resolves a natural scale where existing exponential estimates only bracket the return bias; its constant \(2^{-\lambda}\) is quantitatively distinct from both prior bounds. The joint Poisson finite-cluster profile identifies the structural mechanism and provides a useful boundary-regime law for recursive-tree percolation, with a motivated connection to finite-group mixing.
